angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 695,700 km at 79.56 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.5686 +/- 0.0118 mas (same row, RUWE 0.91): 79.56 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Wood et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 109833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...85W/abstract): 695,700 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.08 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Wood et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 109833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...85W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5881 +/- 50 K from Wood et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 109833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...85W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Wood et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 109833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...85W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-109833.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.471, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
